Alexander Duff
al-ig-ZAN-der DUFF
proper noun
Scottish; Alexander from the Greek Alexandros, “defender of men,” and Duff, a Highland surname from the Gaelic dubh, “dark.” Borne by the pioneering missionary-educator of India (1806–1878).

Biblical Definition

Alexander Duff, the first missionary sent abroad by the Church of Scotland, reached Calcutta in 1830 after twice suffering shipwreck on the passage, his library lost to the sea both times save for a Bible that floated to shore. Persuaded that the strongholds of Hindu learning must be met on the ground of learning itself, he established schools in which the whole compass of Western knowledge was taught, yet always as the handmaid of the truth, that the light of the gospel might break in upon the darkened understanding of the highest castes. He set the English tongue and the sciences at the service of Christ, reasoning that a false religion propped upon a false view of the world would fall when the true view of God’s creation was set before it, crowned always by the Scriptures. Many of the earliest and most notable converts of Bengal came through his lecture-hall, and his method shaped Protestant educational missions across India for a century. His life preaches that the gospel does not fear the schoolroom but sanctifies it, that every faculty of man is to be brought captive to the obedience of Christ, and that the LORD raises up learned men to storm the citadels of learned error. Returning broken in health to Scotland, Duff pleaded the cause of missions until his death, a defender of men indeed, but chiefly a servant of the God who defends His own.

Webster 1828 Definition

The pioneer of Christian higher education as a missionary method in India.

expand to see more

A Scot (1806–1878), first foreign missionary of the Church of Scotland, sent to Bengal in 1830.

Founder of a system of Christian schools teaching Western learning as the servant of the gospel.

Survivor of two shipwrecks on his outward voyages, his floated Bible a token of providence.

An advocate whose plea for missions stirred the churches of Scotland and beyond.

A pioneer whose educational method shaped Protestant missions across India for generations.

Key Scripture

2Co 10:5 — "Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ;"

Pro 4:7 — "Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding."

Dan 12:3 — "And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever."

Psa 119:130 — "The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple."

Modern Corruption

A faithful witness, not a contested doctrine; his life recovers the principle that all true learning is subject to Christ.

expand to see more

Duff’s memory is preserved not as a disputed teaching but as a standing witness that the gospel need not retreat before the learning of the world. He met the pride of Hindu scholarship not by shunning knowledge but by consecrating it, that the light of Scripture might expose the darkness of idolatry.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover from Duff’s labour is that wisdom is the principal thing and that every high thing which exalts itself against the knowledge of God must be cast down and brought captive to the obedience of Christ. His schools stand against the notion that faith and understanding are enemies, and remind the church that the God who made the mind commands its worship.

Hebrew Roots

A defender-of-men by name who found his root in the wisdom that begins with the fear of the LORD.

expand to see more

Alexander — Greek Alexandros, “defender of men,” borne fitly by a contender for truth.

Duff — Gaelic dubh, “dark,” yet he carried light into darkness.

The root of wisdom: the fear of the LORD (Pro 9:10), which he set above all learning.

Grounded in 2Co 10:5, bringing every thought captive to Christ.

A star turning many to righteousness, promised to shine for ever (Dan 12:3).

Usage

"Named as the pioneer of educational missions, teaching Western science under the lordship of Christ."

"Cited for the principle that learning must be sanctified, not feared, in the service of the gospel."

"Remembered for the shipwrecks in which his Bible alone was preserved to him."
